body:
## Symptom
Per-item crypto cost grows with the number of stored items, so any path that decrypts a bounded set of rows still slows down as a bank grows.

## Where
- `crates/clio-store/src/dek.rs:263` `LocalDevKms::decrypt` calls `self.refresh(&mut slots)` before every lookup.
- `crates/clio-store/src/dek.rs:184` `refresh` does `*slots = load_slots(path)?` — reads and parses the entire key JSON file each call.
- `ensure_dek` (`dek.rs:223`) and `encrypt` (`dek.rs:237`) do the same.
- The file grows because the CLI creates one DEK per item: `build_item` sets `subject_id` to the item id when the caller omits one, so every `remember` adds a new subject slot.

## Impact
Each `get_memory_item` decrypt is O(key-file size). Measured on a file-backed SQLite DB with the default profile:

- `clio admit` (bounded scan of 64 rows) at 300 items: ~0.29s; at 600 items: ~0.40s; the delta tracks the key file doubling (33KB -> 67KB).
- Before the #6 fix the same path decrypted the whole bank twice; that was ~2.2s at 588 items. The #6 fix bounded the decrypt count to 64, but each decrypt is still O(n), so the write path remains linear in bank size.

## Proposed fix
- Keep the slot map in memory and only reload on a miss, on a version/`mtime` change, or on an explicit invalidation; do not reload on every call.
- If cross-process freshness is required, gate the reload on file `mtime`/size rather than unconditional reparse.
- Alternatively, persist DEKs per subject so the file does not grow with item count (for example a fixed per-bank DEK when the caller omits `subject_id`).

Discovered while fixing #6; not changed there to keep that fix scoped.
title: LocalDevKms reloads and reparses the whole key file on every decrypt/encrypt
